sequences.title: Ministry of Jesus
sequences.note: From John's preaching to the week of the Passion, ordered by what the Gospels say came before what rather than dated. Mark's order is the backbone of the Galilean ministry, John's feasts and notes of time frame the whole, and Luke's order places what he alone tells. Where the Gospels part ways — Mark and Luke on when the fishermen were called, Matthew's gathering of the miracles in chapters 8 and 9 — one order is kept and the other left out. A. T. Robertson's *Harmony of the Gospels* (1922) is a further witness: where its order agrees with the Gospels' an ordering rests on both, and where it orders what they leave open it rests on Robertson alone. Two of its placements are not taken: John's beheading, which Robertson tells where Herod hears of Jesus (Mark tells it looking back), and the anointing at Bethany, which Robertson sets two days before the Passover with Mark and Matthew where John has it six days before. Events no line joins are of unknown order to one another. Estimated sites are working reconstructions from surrounding passages. Chorazin records retrospectively attested activity with no dated position. The priests' council is not part of Jesus' travel track; Siloam is the healed man's destination.

sequences.title: Birth and childhood of Jesus
sequences.note: The birth and childhood of Jesus, the Son of God, with the birth of John the Baptist. Matthew 1-2 and Luke 1-2 supply separate chains. No order is asserted between the visit of the wise men and the presentation in the temple. Luke summarises the return to Nazareth without relating the flight into Egypt; both accounts lead into the childhood in Nazareth. Dates on the overview are inherited from the source chronology, not supplied by these chains. Map pins mark places named in the account, not an exact travel route. Events spanning several regions have no single region lane; unnamed locations are left unpinned. The Egyptian refuge is a regional estimate in the eastern Nile delta. The return-from-Egypt node marks the departure region; the next Nazareth node gives the recorded destination. Temple events use an estimated point within the precinct.

sequences.title: Acts of the apostles
sequences.note: The gospel of the Kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ spreads from Jerusalem towards Rome (Acts 1:8; 8:12; 28:30-31). Ecclesia means the assembly of believers; the Holy Spirit is God's power, poured out to equip the apostles as witnesses (Acts 1:8; 2:17-18). The journeys open their own sequences. Chains follow connected narratives; Peter's work and the scattered brethren are not forced into the order of Paul's movements. The date of Galatians relative to the journeys and council is disputed, so its writing is left unordered here. Overview years are inherited from the source chronology. Map pins mark places named in the account, not an exact travel route. Events spanning several regions have no single region lane; unnamed locations are left unpinned.
